source_scope: 17 selected production, ABI, adapter, test and build inputs match the Linux workspace byte-for-byte; not a hermetic whole-worktree release manifest.

execution.runtime: native root host CLI, two private network namespaces with MTU-1500 veth, one selected cgroup, persistent IPv4/IPv6 UDP sockets

findings.change: Add native persistent-worker network loss acceptance with independent selected-port TC counters and exact per-endpoint packet multisets. Share network namespace/socket setup with the earlier MTU test. No product runtime fix needed.
findings.interpretation: Complete capture means hook observation delivery is accounted for, not that a peer received every datagram. TC egress drops after the sender hook cause application timeouts without collector loss. Received facts are never filled from the oracle.
development_attempts: attempt-1: normal receive deadline too short for fresh neighbors; corrected to 3 seconds while keeping only injected timeout paths at 350ms
attempt-2: actual TC uses flat stats.packets/stats.drops, not assumed nested basic/queue fields; corrected parser and added wrong-port rejection

summary_projection: Expected packet prefix arrays and network-regression observation arrays are omitted here; original worker oracles, exports and full summaries remain under evidence_root. Hashes bind those original summary bytes, not this projection.

validation.clippy_command: cargo --config profile.dev.package.gewyvern.opt-level=2 clippy --locked --test production_capture_linux_tdd --test native_validation_harness_tdd -- -D warnings
validation.status_validation_scope: Catalog consistency and declared GUI target coverage, not overall product readiness.

limits: One host, private veth and deterministic selected-port UDP drops, not random loss, reordering, congestion, ICMP/PMTU, physical links or high load.
TC counters and test coordination establish the fixture's drop location; no automatic product root-cause classifier or remote-delivery guarantee.
All fault-test payloads are 32 bytes. This does not change the product's 128-byte payload prefix limit.
Namespace identities are run-local and process lineage remains unverified.
The lifecycle control intentionally loses records and remains incomplete; SIGKILL cannot produce final complete counters.
No release-artifact, protocol-count or status-maturity promotion.
